title: Segment hinting and stochastic prefetch controller for paged KV residency
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: High variability in decode latency for long-context workloads caused by aggressive prefill and coarse-grained residency decisions. Current prefill pipeline frequently pulls entire large KV pages for short-lived spans, causing decode stalls and cross-tenant thrashing. Goal: Implement a segment-hinting layer + stochastic prefetch controller that (1) provides per-request lightweight hints about likely token spans, (2) guides the prefill controller to admit only probabilistically selected sub-pages, and (3) exposes residency signals to the kernel selection layer so we can preferentially schedule kernels that tolerate partial KV coverage. This work touches allocation, eviction, fragmentation, and reuse: we will add a hint bitset per request, a small sampled prefetch budget per tenant, and a segment-level age score used by eviction. Deliverables: algorithm, runtime adapter, metrics, simulation harness, integration tests, and a canary rollout plan. Integration points: decode scheduler (admission), kernel-selector (fallback to partial-KV kernels), allocator (segment-level quotas), and console metrics (per-tenant prefill accept/reject rates).
acceptance_criteria: 95th-percentile decode latency improved by >=15% on our long-context benchmark (>=8k tokens) compared to baseline prefill
Prefill-induced stalls (measured as decode waiting for KV page) reduced by >=40% in synthetic multi-tenant replay
No increase in overall model token cost >5% for production traffic mix
Automated simulator reproduces eviction/reuse behavior and matches live bench traces within 10% of page admission ratios
Design doc approved by runtime and infra leads and PRs merged with tests and perf baselines
technical_notes: Segment hinting: compute a compact 64-bit bloom-like fingerprint for the predicted span, attach as request hint header. Hints are advisory only.
Stochastic prefetch controller: per-tenant token-weighted sampler that converts hints + occupancy to a probability p_admit, uses reservoir sampling for admission when multiple segments compete.
Residency bookkeeping: shift from page-level LRU to a segment-occupancy histogram. Each segment has an age_score = touch_count / (1 + last_touch_delta) used by eviction comparator.

Kernel integration: when partial segments are present, trigger kernel variant that supports sparse KV loads (lower memory locality but avoids full-page stall). Fallback scheduling when admission fails.
Avoiding fragmentation blowup: coalesce adjacent hot subsegments periodically using background compaction limited by GPU memory stableness threshold.
Safety: admission decisions cannot increase tenant quota beyond configurable soft limit; controller has backpressure signal to decode scheduler.
Metrics: per-tenant admitted_segments, rejected_segments, stall_time_ms, kernel_fallback_count, compaction_runs
Configuration knobs: segment_size_bytes, admit_window_ms, sampling_rate, tenant_soft_quota

2025-03-06 — Claire Ng (review): Suggests adding kernel fallback metric and ensuring admission does not violate tenant soft-quota under bursty traffic. Also asked for a compaction safety cutoff to avoid interfering with live decodes.

2025-03-11 — Miguel Torres: Ran multi-tenant replay with revised sampling_rate=0.25; observed 42% reduction in prefill-induced stalls and 9% reduction in p95 decode latency. Tenant fairness looked stable.

2025-03-12 — Asha Patel: Preparing canary rollout doc and dashboard (links attached). Need sign-off from infra and runtime on safe default knobs. Next: finalize compaction heuristics and run longer 24h stability replay.
rollout_plan: Start with internal canary (10% of internal traffic) for 48h, monitor stall_time_ms and kernel_fallback_count. If stable, escalate to 2 customer tenants with dedicated capacity for 72h. Gradual ramp to 25% of production in weekly increments with automatic rollback on >10% regression in p95 latency or increase in OOM events.
test_plan: Unit tests for hint encoding/decoding and admission logic
Simulator that replays historical traces with configurable sampling_rate and occupancy limits
Perf harness: end-to-end long-context bench comparing baseline vs controller across 3 model families
Stress test: bursty multi-tenant replay for 24h to measure fragmentation and compaction impact
